issues.issue: Step (c) wall-time measurement runs, done before FREEZE, will print test MSE for the scored configurations. 'Step (c) measures epochs-to-stop and s/epoch per arm' needs full training runs at H=192/336 under the released loop, which prints the test loss every epoch and the final test mse/mae, and appends them to a result file. If those runs use a seed in S (e.g. 2021, the released default) they are, up to determinism, the scored runs themselves, seen before the design is frozen. Nothing in sec.8 keeps those numbers away from the people who still finalise the prereg (FREEZE transcription of margins, resumable-state decision, any engineering choice).
issues.evidence: tfps exp/exp_main.py:258 (test pass every epoch), :260-261 (prints Test Loss), :383-390 (prints and appends mse to ./result_*.txt); run_longExp.py:163 (exp.test after train); official exp_main.py:200-203. PREREG sec.8 lines 275-278 (step (c) measures epochs-to-stop per arm), sec.8 line 280 (budget 'replaced by step (c) measurements'). Precedent: audits/tfps/feas_zero.log and feas_orth.log already show test losses (H=96, 3 epochs, seed 2021, lr 5e-4; not a scored config).
issues.fix: Add to sec.8: step (c) timing/feasibility runs use a seed outside S and outside the extension set (e.g. 999), are never scored, and their stdout passes through a filter that drops lines containing 'Test Loss' and 'mse:' (and the wrapper deletes ./result_*.txt and test_results/ after the run); epochs-to-stop is read from the filtered log. Record in STATE.md that no H=192/336 test number was seen before FREEZE. Also disclose in sec.2 or sec.9 that the H=96 feasibility logs (feas_zero/feas_orth, 3 epochs) exposed two test MSEs at a horizon outside the scored set.

issues.issue: Seed collision between eval-noise draws and the D generators. Eval draw k uses global seed 10000k+seed, so k=3 gives 30000+seed (the time-D generator seed) and k=4 gives 40000+seed (the frequency-D generator seed), for every seed. torch's CPU generator gives the same normal stream for the same seed whether global or dedicated, so the 'fresh' router noise in draws 3 and 4 is largely a shifted copy of the D initial values (G) of arms 1-2. Probe (torch 2.4.1 CPU, seed 2021): global manual_seed(32021) then randn(1536,4) equals randn(112,112) from Generator(32021) exactly (100% of entries); with one int64 draw first (what a DataLoader iterator consumes), 75% of entries equal G at a shift of 2. Effect on scores is probably negligible (each noise value is one of 12544 D entries), but draws 3 and 4 are not independent of arm 1/2's initialisation as the design assumes, and it is free to avoid.
issues.evidence: PREREG sec.5 lines 111-112 (30000+seed, 40000+seed) vs sec.6 line 146 (10000k+seed, k=1..5); SparseMoE.py:59 (torch.randn_like on the global RNG); probe run in this review (no training).
issues.fix: Change the eval-noise seeds to a disjoint range, e.g. 1_000_000 + 10000k + seed (or D generators to 7_000_000+seed / 8_000_000+seed), and add a self-test in sec.8 asserting that the sets {training seeds}, {D generator seeds}, {eval-noise seeds} are pairwise disjoint for S and the extension seeds.

issues.issue: The pure-val-MSE checkpoint is the min of val MSE over the epochs that the released criterion lets the run reach, not an early stop on val MSE. Its candidate set therefore differs by arm: under arm 1 the aux term keeps falling, so the run can go much longer (up to 100 epochs) and the val-MSE min is taken over more noisy (one router-noise draw per epoch) candidates than under arm 3. This is a val-side budget difference, not test leakage, but the sensitivity is not the 'pure-val-MSE early stopping' a reader might assume. Tie handling is also unstated.
issues.evidence: tfps exp/exp_main.py:257,262-265 (stop decided on total val loss); utils/tools.py:50-63; PREREG sec.6 lines 153-155.
issues.fix: Sec.6: state 'checkpoint_valmse = epoch with the lowest val MSE among epochs 1..stop epoch of the released criterion; ties to the earliest epoch', and print the per-arm mean number of candidate epochs next to the pure-val-MSE table (already logged as epochs-to-stop).

issues.issue: Published-lr qualifier (owner decision 11) is under-specified in three places: (a) 'if it does not hold there' does not say whether a more negative published-lr label (e.g. REVERSED where the searched label is VANISHES) counts as holding; (b) no rule for a published-lr run that is non-finite while the seed is not failed under the search rule (a baseline seed fails only if all 4 lr runs fail); (c) the name 'published lr' omits that the other published settings differ (DLinear script batch 32, both scripts seq_len 336, patience 100).
issues.evidence: PREREG sec.5 lines 134-139, sec.7 lines 214-217; patchtst_official scripts/PatchTST/etth1.sh:42 (lr 1e-4, batch 128, seq_len 336 at :8), scripts/Linear/etth1.sh:24,38,52 (lr 5e-3, batch 32, seq_len 336 at :9); official run_longExp.py:80 (patience 100).
issues.fix: Sec.7: 'holds' = published-lr horizon label is in {REVERSED, VANISHES, SHRINKS} and at least as negative as the searched label (order REVERSED < VANISHES < SHRINKS). Sec.6: in the published-lr table a non-finite run at the published lr is a failed run for that table, with the same BLOCKED/n=4 rules. Label text: 'published-lr (lr from the PatchTST repo scripts; L=96, batch 128, patience 20 as sec.5)'.

issues.issue: No self-test that the instrumentation (val-pass hook, criterion/loader wrapping, EarlyStopping subclass, extra checkpoint save) leaves training unchanged. A hook that re-implements vali() or calls the model again would shift the global RNG stream (router noise SparseMoE.py:59, val shuffle) and silently make the audited runs differ from the released loop, differently by arm.

issues.issue: Baseline 'full float' val_loss_min is float32, not float64: the official vali() averages a list of 0-d float32 tensors with np.average, which returns numpy.float32 (checked). Exact ties between lr runs are improbable but less so than the text implies; the tie rule covers it.

summary: All r2 leakage/selection/budget issues are fixed: the val-loader-keyed hook with RNG save/restore, the EarlyStopping subclass, --itr 1, absolute-path loading, the NaN rule, the committed width-only extension trigger, and the disclosed lr asymmetry. No arm selects on test. One major non-blocking gap: step (c) timing runs would print H=192/336 test MSE before FREEZE, possibly on a scored seed, so they need an off-set seed and filtered output. Minor: the eval-noise seeds for k=3/4 equal the D generator seeds (probe: the noise is a shifted copy of G); the pure-val-MSE candidate set and ties are unstated; the published-lr qualifier is underdefined; the routing-measurement draw is unstated; there is no non-interference self-test; baseline val loss is float32.
